content:
anya_prod: quick heads-up — sales escalated a customer ask: they want a blended pricing option across reserved + burst capacity. customer is a fintech doing ~3B tokens/month, wants 40% of usage as reserved commit and 60% burstable credits with lower overage rates.

kai_sales: customer says their procurement will only sign if they get predictable unit cost across both modes. they asked for a single effective per-token rate and rollover credits for unused reserved capacity.

chris_finops: rough math from their numbers: if reserved 40% = 1.2B tokens/mo, and we price reserved at $0.0012/token and burst at $0.0020/token, blended rate ~ $0.00176/token. they asked for 10% discount to that blended rate.

leo_engineering: concerns: supporting a blended SLA/rolling credits mix impacts routing and billing. we'll need policy that routes to reserved pool first, then burst, and a clear accounting signal per request. easy to track via route tags but impacts cache locality.

sam_support: also flagged that support will get more questions if we allow rollover credits. we need docs + UI language for how credits expire and visibility in console.

anya_prod: proposed product ask: create a "Commit + Burst Blended" packaging option with:
- defined commit % buckets (25/40/60)
- explicit effective blended rate calculation in billing UI
- one-time opt-in for rollover up to 3 months, forfeitable on churn
- can only be attached to dedicated pools (for latency SLAs)

kai_sales: sales needs a playbook snippet we can use in negotiations: negotiation levers, example numbers, and what engineering must guarantee.

leo_engineering: technical acceptance criteria I'd need:
1) request-level metadata emitted: `billing.mode` = {"reserved","burst","blended"}
2) routing policy: reserved-first, fallback to burst with X retries
3) telemetry: per-route token counters and 7d aggregated view in console

chris_finops: billing acceptance criteria:
- blended rate calc matches sample spreadsheet
- rollover accounting visible in invoices
- credits burn order documented (reserved -> rollover -> burst)

anya_prod: launch criteria draft:
- product + finance sign-off on pricing table
- engineering implements telemetry + routing policy in staging and one e2e test customer
- support + docs ready with FAQ and refund/playbook
- legal reviews T&C for rollover credits

tina_legal: flagged: rollover credits wording needs clarity on liability on termination. we need a TTL and a clear forfeiture clause. also confirm whether credits are transferable.

kai_sales: customer also asked about a soft overage cap: if monthly bursts exceed 120% of committed burst plan, auto-notify and cap at negotiated rate. is that doable?

leo_engineering: we can implement alerting and soft-throttles at the routing layer. hard caps are trickier because they can cause failures; prefer notifications + auto-escalation to overflow region or lower-cost variant.

chris_finops: from pricing perspective, offering a hard cap at negotiated rate means we absorb delta risk. need exec approval for that exposure.

anya_prod: ok next steps:
- product to own spec doc + sample pricing spreadsheet (i'll draft) — due EOW
- eng to prototype `billing.mode` tagging & routing change in sandbox — @leo_engineering please confirm feasibility by Wed
- finops to produce P&L scenarios for 3 discount bands (5/10/15%) — @chris_finops due Thu
- legal to draft rollover language template — @tina_legal due Fri
- sales to gather procurement timeline & ask customer for their acceptance criteria — @kai_sales pls update thread with that timeline

sam_support: i'll start a draft FAQ and a support runbook for common edge cases (double-billing, credit visibility).

ops-bot: deployment queue updated: feature-flag `blended-packaging` created in sandbox.

leo_engineering: confirming feasibility: tagging + metrics straightforward; rollout risk is around routing + cache-locality. will need an A/B canary gated by token-rate thresholds.

anya_prod: great. if no objections i'll spin up the spec doc and link it here when done. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

kai_sales: noted — will ping with procurement timeline today

chris_finops: one quick ask: include sample invoice line items in the spreadsheet so finance ops can validate ingestion.

anya_prod: will include. final note: keep the packaging modular — we shouldn't hardwire blended logic into core runtime until metrics justify it. prefer feature-flagged beta.

leo_engineering: agreed. start small, measure unit economics, iterate.

sam_support: tagging docs when ready.

tina_legal: will circulate draft language.

anya_prod: thread summary: action owners + due dates above. next sync if any blocker: Friday standup.

kai_sales: thanks all.
